"""Core task operations. due_at throughout this module is in SECONDS, matching models.Task."""
import re
import time

from tinytasks.models import Task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all, next_id, save_all


EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+")


def create_task(title: str, due_in_seconds: float) -> Task:
    """Create a task due `due_in_seconds` seconds from now."""
    tasks = load_all()
    task = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=EMAIL_RE.sub("[email]", title), due_at=time.time() + due_in_seconds)
    tasks.append(task)
    save_all(tasks)
    return task


def get_overdue_tasks(now: float | None = None) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks whose due_at (seconds) has already passed."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    return [t for t in load_all() if t.due_at < now]


def delete_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    tasks = load_all()
    remaining = [t for t in tasks if t.id != task_id]
    save_all(remaining)

def test_export_cli_excludes_archived_tasks(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import subprocess, sys, json
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("keep", due_in_seconds=60)
    old = create_task("gone", due_in_seconds=60)
    archive_task(old.id)
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "tinytasks.cli", "export"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    assert [d["title"] for d in json.loads(out)] == ["keep"]


def test_add_redacts_email_in_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("call jo.smith+x@example.co.uk and bob@a.com today", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert load_all()[0].title == "call [email] and [email] today"


def test_reschedule_rejects_past_due_date(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import pytest
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("x", due_in_seconds=60)
    original = load_all()[0].due_at
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        reschedule_task(t.id, -5)
    assert load_all()[0].due_at == original


def test_reschedule_cli_past_exits_nonzero_and_leaves_task(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import subprocess, sys
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("x", due_in_seconds=60)
    original = load_all()[0].due_at
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "tinytasks.cli", "reschedule", str(t.id), "--due-in", "-5"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert r.returncode != 0
    assert load_all()[0].due_at == original


def test_tags_stored_lowercase_and_deduped(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("tagged", due_in_seconds=60)
    add_tags(t.id, ["Urgent", "urgent", "Work"])
    assert load_all()[0].tags == ["urgent", "work"]

`add` now stores the title exactly as typed, so email addresses stay in it. The suite passes (13 tests), and the change is committed as `18d92e2`.

- **Code:** I removed the email redaction from `create_task` in `tinytasks/api.py`, along with the regex it used.
- **Test:** `test_add_redacts_email_in_title` is now `test_add_keeps_email_in_title`. It checks that a title with two addresses comes back unchanged.
- **CLAUDE.md:** I replaced the C2 rule with the new behavior and noted that it deliberately overrides the Compliance memo (draft v0.3).

This reverses Compliance memo C2, which required replacing emails with `[email]`. I didn't find any compliance sign-off for dropping it, and CLAUDE.md now says so. Customer emails will now be stored in plain text and show up in `export` output. You may want to check with the Compliance Office, and with Priya Raman if the product spec is affected, before this ships.
